harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as the DHCP server on the private network it shares with node2 and node3 (eth1/ens7/ens7, subnet 10.50.50.0/24, pool .100-.200), and configured node2/node3 to obtain that interface's address via DHCP instead of remaining unconfigured/static, all implemented via an Ansible playbook run from node4 (the only node with Ansible pre-installed, hence the control node). Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart-and-recovery pass on all 4 managed nodes.
actions_performed: Surveyed all 4 nodes: node1=VyOS (eth0 default net + eth1 unconfigured private NIC), node2/node3=Ubuntu 16.04 (ens2 default net + ens7 unconfigured private NIC), node4=Ubuntu 24.04 with ansible-core 2.20.5 pre-installed (the designated control_node)
Wired passwordless SSH from node4 to node1 (vyos user), node2 and node3 (antrieb user, passwordless sudo) using CLUSTER_SSH_PUBKEY/PRIVKEY
Built /root/ansible-dhcp/{inventory.ini, ansible.cfg, playbook.yml} on node4

Diagnosed and fixed a VyOS gotcha: running VyOS configure/set/commit as root/sudo corrupts the vyattacfg group config session ('Set failed' until reboot); switched to 'sg vyattacfg -c' as the vyos user per VyOS docs, and recovered node1 with a reboot to clear the corrupted session before applying real config

Corrected the DHCP-server config syntax for this VyOS build's current schema (subnet-id + range/option nodes, not the older subnet-parameters/default-router/name-server syntax) by inspecting the on-node CLI templates

Play 1 (dhcp_server/node1): renders and applies a VyOS script setting eth1=10.50.50.1/24 and a Kea-backed DHCP server (LAN shared-network, subnet 10.50.50.0/24, range .100-.200, default-router/name-server options), commits and saves; verified via 'show dhcp server statistics'

Play 2 (dhcp_clients/node2,node3): since these Ubuntu 16.04 hosts only have Python 2.7/3.5 (incompatible with ansible-core 2.20's module payloads), used ansible.builtin.raw to write /etc/network/interfaces.d/ens7.cfg ('iface ens7 inet dhcp') and ifdown/ifup ens7
Ran the playbook twice to confirm idempotency and correct lease assignment (node2=10.50.50.100, node3=10.50.50.101)
Captured a healthy baseline (boot_id, DHCP service state, leases, interface addresses, cross-node pings) on all 4 nodes

Restarted node2, node3, node1, then node4 one at a time (never concurrently), polling each until command execution resumed, proving a changed boot_id each time, and re-verifying DHCP server health/leases and client connectivity after each restart
Re-ran the Ansible playbook post-reboot from node4 to confirm the control node and its playbook/inventory persisted and the whole flow remains reproducible

evidence.requirement: node1 shares a private, previously-unconfigured network with node2/node3 (not node4)
evidence.summary: ip -4/-br addr and ip link across all 4 nodes show node1/eth1, node2/ens7, node3/ens7 as a second, unaddressed NIC on a shared subnet while node4 has only one NIC

evidence.requirement: control_node identification for the Ansible-based implementation
evidence.summary: Only node4 has ansible/ansible-playbook installed (ansible-core 2.20.5); node1-3 lack it, confirming node4 as the configured control_node used to orchestrate the others

evidence.requirement: DHCP server configured on node1 via Ansible
evidence.summary: playbook.yml on node4 renders and applies the VyOS DHCP-server config via sg vyattacfg; node1's 'show dhcp server statistics' and config.boot confirm a live Kea DHCPv4 pool (LAN, 10.50.50.0/24, 101 addresses) after both the first and idempotent second ansible-playbook run

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 configured to obtain their private-network address via DHCP from node1, not static
evidence.summary: Ansible raw tasks wrote /etc/network/interfaces.d/ens7.cfg with 'iface ens7 inet dhcp' and brought the interface up; both nodes leased addresses from node1's pool (10.50.50.100/10.50.50.101) and could ping each other and node1 over the private network

evidence.requirement: node1 restart baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered DHCP service/config/leases
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 1f48c3dd...; reboot acknowledged before disconnect; polled until boot_id became 9d3b2f29... (changed); post-reboot state shows eth1 address, active Kea service, saved dhcp-server config.boot section, and both clients still able to ping node1 over 10.50.50.0/24

evidence.requirement: node2 restart baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered DHCP-client lease/connectivity
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 0d49f077...; reboot acknowledged before disconnect; polled until boot_id became 5fc8894a... (changed); post-reboot ens7 auto-reacquired 10.50.50.100 via the persisted ifupdown config and pinged node1/node3 successfully

evidence.requirement: node3 restart baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered DHCP-client lease/connectivity
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 2b3a8d87...; reboot acknowledged before disconnect; polled until boot_id became 66db5faa... (changed); post-reboot ens7 auto-reacquired 10.50.50.101 and pinged node1/node2 successfully

evidence.requirement: node4 (control node) restart baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered ansible tooling and cluster SSH access
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id d5f5239f...; reboot acknowledged before disconnect; polled until boot_id became cde59737... (changed); post-reboot the /root/ansible-dhcp playbook/inventory persisted and a fresh ansible-playbook run from node4 against all 3 managed nodes succeeded, re-confirming DHCP server/client health end-to-end
